title: Container Bookings: Vessel Rolls by the Carrier and by the Customer
content:
A roll takes a Container Bookings booking off the sailing it was allocated and places it on a later sailing of the same service. This page defines the two kinds of roll and the money that follows each.

## What counts as a roll, and who causes it

- **Carrier roll.** Caused by overbooking, a blank sailing or a port omission. On an overbooked sailing the line rolls bookings starting from the highest loading priority rank number and working downwards, so that rank 1 is rolled last. Overbooking never rolls a booking whose product guarantees space; such a booking moves only when its sailing is blanked or its port is omitted.
- **Customer roll.** Caused by the customer asking for another sailing, or by documents that arrived after grace under the documentation cut-off rules.

Each roll is logged as one roll notice on the booking's charge history, showing the sailing the booking was taken off and whether the carrier or the customer caused it. The booking's vessel and voyage, its scheduled departure date and its three cut-offs are replaced with those of the new sailing.

## Compensation for carrier rolls: clauses in force

Only a roll whose roll notice records the carrier as its cause can earn compensation. The credit is limited so that the compensation already credited on the booking, together with the new credit, never goes beyond the product's per-booking compensation ceiling. A product whose per-container compensation is 0.00 earns no credit and no entry is written. A carrier roll can be compensated once and no more. Carrier rolls never bear a fee, and they count towards the product's figure for fee-free cancellation.

## Fees for customer rolls: clauses in force

A customer roll is accepted only while the customer rolls already recorded on the booking number fewer than the product's maximum; beyond that the customer has to cancel under the cancellation rules and book again. A customer roll is free while the booking's count of customer rolls, the one being handled included, does not exceed the product's free customer rolls. A chargeable customer roll is written as an amendment-fee entry coded as a customer roll fee, of the amendment kind "customer-requested vessel change".

## Clauses no longer in force

- Crediting a compensated carrier roll at the product's per-container compensation multiplied by the booking's whole container quantity is no longer in force.
- Admitting a carrier roll to compensation whenever the booking's carrier-roll count, that roll included, did not exceed the product's number of compensated rolls is no longer in force.
- Pricing a chargeable customer roll on the booking's entire container quantity, at the product's customer roll rate for each container, is no longer in force.

Each of these has been superseded by the current basis for crediting roll compensation or for charging the customer roll fee, as the case may be.

## Basis Q&A

**Does a roll forced by late documents count as the customer's roll?** Yes; documents arriving after grace make the resulting roll a customer roll.

**Can a guaranteed-space booking be rolled because the ship is overbooked?** No; only a blank sailing or a port omission can roll it.

**Hypothetical acceptance check.** Under an invented maximum of 2 customer rolls, a booking already showing 1 customer roll may take another; a booking already showing 2 may not, and the customer would need to cancel and rebook.
